title: School-Based Health Center Consent (Texas)
about: A parent's or guardian's written consent for a student to be seen at a school-based health center in Texas, by each kind of service the center gives, ongoing or for one visit. List your center's services under each kind before you use it. A center funded by a Texas SBHC grant may not give reproductive services, counseling or referrals (Education Code 38.055).

blocks.text: {facility.name} runs the health center at your child's school. Texas law says we may see your child only with the written consent of a parent, a guardian or another person having legal control of the student.
These are all the kinds of services our center gives. Check each kind you agree to. The list below each kind says what we give.

blocks.label: What we give in each kind
For how long
items: Ongoing services, until the end of this school year
Only on a single occasion, on the date below

blocks.text: Some visits use a questionnaire about feelings, habits or health, such as one for depression. Texas law says we need your consent first. We will give you a copy of each questionnaire before we use it.

items: I do not agree to questionnaires

blocks.text: If your child needs physical or mental health care somewhere else, we will tell you why. We will talk with you and tell you in writing. We refer your child only after you agree in writing to that type of care, for each visit or for a course of treatment.
We share your child's health information with anyone other than you only with your written consent, unless a law allows it. You may see your child's health records and get a copy.

If your child has a primary care physician, we tell them about the care we give, so their records stay complete. If your child has Medicaid, CHIP or private insurance, we contact the physician before we give care.
You can change or withdraw this consent at any time. Tell us in writing.

signers: Parent, guardian or other person having legal control of the student
